message: Command `cat /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/libpcap/testprogs/fuzz/fuzz_pcap.c && echo "===" && grep -n "pcap_usb_header_mmapped" /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/libpcap/pcap/usb.h | head -5 && sed -n '/pcap_usb_header_mmapped/,/^}/p' /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/libpcap/pcap/usb.h` executed with exit code 0.

message.content:
Now I understand the vulnerability. In `fixup_pcap_pkthdr()`, the code accesses `usb_hdr->data_flag`, `usb_hdr->ndesc`, and `usb_hdr->urb_len` without first checking that `hdr->caplen` is at least `sizeof(pcap_usb_header_mmapped)`. This means if the captured data is shorter than the USB header, it will read out of bounds.

Let me look at the fuzz target and the USB header structure to understand the input format.
